Contributing

Source: CONTRIBUTING.md

Feedback, bug reports, and ideas are welcome through GitHub issues.

Who can do what

  • Anyone with a GitHub account can open issues and comment on them.
  • Members of the NCC-CNC Cons-Tech team develop the package: the team has write access, so members push branches and open and merge pull requests, all with the same rights. Org owners also have admin through their org role, for repo settings.
  • Anyone else who wants to propose a change can fork the repo and open a pull request from the fork; a team member merges it by hand.

To develop the package, ask an org owner to add you to the Cons-Tech team. Access to this repo is through the team, not individual grants.

Workflow

The workflow is:

  1. Branch from dev, the integration branch (one short-lived branch per change). main, the default branch, holds the latest release.
  2. Keep changes small and focused.
  3. Run the package checks locally before pushing (see Setup below).
  4. Open a pull request into dev (choose dev as the base; GitHub offers main by default). CI must pass before merge. A PR into dev from a branch in this repo merges itself (squash) once CI passes, and is kept up to date with dev while it waits; this is done by the NCC ConsTech Automation app (.github/workflows/auto-merge.yml and update-branches.yml). Open it as a draft to hold it back.
  5. Do not open pull requests into main. main changes only by a promotion PR from dev, opened when the owner asks, usually for a release (ADR 0024). Promotion PRs are not auto-merged: the owner merges them by hand with “Create a merge commit” (not squash or rebase).

Setup

Prerequisites:

  • R 4.4 or later.
  • The devtools, styler, lintr and covr packages: install.packages(c("devtools", "styler", "lintr", "covr")). Rtools is not needed while the package has no compiled code.

From the repo root:

Rscript -e "devtools::install_deps(dependencies = TRUE)"  # package dependencies
Rscript -e "styler::style_pkg()"     # format R code
Rscript -e "lintr::lint_package()"   # lint
Rscript -e "devtools::document()"    # regenerate man/ and NAMESPACE; commit them
Rscript -e "devtools::test()"        # run the tests
Rscript -e "devtools::check()"       # full R CMD check (build, tests, examples)
Rscript -e "pkgdown::check_pkgdown()" # site config lists every exported topic

The pkgdown check needs the pkgdown package and pandoc (RStudio bundles one; set RSTUDIO_PANDOC to its folder if pandoc is not on the path). Rscript -e "pkgdown::build_site()" previews the reference site in site/, which is not committed. The published site, https://ncc-cnc.github.io/constechr/, is built from release tags only (ADR 0025): pushing a vX.Y.Z tag publishes it.

A release takes two manual steps (ADR 0028): bump the version in a PR into dev (usethis::use_version("patch"), "minor" or "major", with its NEWS.md entry; for a release of one change, that change’s PR can carry it), then open and merge the promotion PR from dev into main. On the merge, release.yml tags the merge commit vX.Y.Z to match DESCRIPTION, and the tag deploys the site. A promotion that leaves the version unchanged tags nothing.

CI runs the same checks on every pull request and weekly: styler::style_pkg(dry = "fail"), the lint, the pkgdown config check, and R CMD check (which runs the tests) on Windows with all dependencies and without Suggests, and on Ubuntu in a pinned rocker/geospatial container. Every job uses the current CRAN version of each dependency, including the recommended packages R ships with, such as Matrix (ADR 0022). Any formatting change, lint, or check error or warning fails it, so if these pass locally CI should too. The Ubuntu check job also runs the formatting check and the lint, and reports test coverage (covr::package_coverage()) in its log. To try the working copy from another repo, install it with Rscript -e "devtools::install()".

See CLAUDE.md for the package’s stack, scope and working rules.

Conventions

  • Conventional Commits (for example feat: ..., fix: ..., chore: ..., docs: ...).
  • No em dashes in code, comments, docs, commit messages, or user-facing text.
  • A change that alters a function’s results or arguments gets a NEWS.md entry under a # constechr (development version) heading at the top (add the heading if it is not there). Do not change Version in DESCRIPTION; it changes only for a release (ADR 0004).
  • NEWS.md has one # constechr x.y.z heading per release, newest first, as usethis::use_version(), pkgdown and utils::news() expect. For a release, usethis::use_version("patch") (or "minor", "major") bumps DESCRIPTION and turns the development heading into the new version’s heading, in one PR into dev just before the promotion PR. Earlier versions, up to 0.2.0, also have headings for development versions between releases. markdownlint’s MD025 (one top-level heading per file) is turned off for NEWS.md only, by the <!-- markdownlint-disable-file MD025 --> comment at its top; keep that line first.
  • See CLAUDE.md for the full working rules and docs/ for design notes and decision records.
